role: builder observation; not independent craft approval

observations.whole: Head/gaze, full cat, guitar and other known paw/material problems remain; without physical specular spots the eyes read flatter.
observations.head: The objectionable horizontal dark/cloudy layer visible in A is no longer visible in D; the bright corneal catchlights are absent. D still has a smooth dark central pupil and blue radial ring.
observations.comparison_to_B_C: Qualitatively similar flattened eye, though D retains non-unit IOR and a nominal refracting shell, so it is not identical to simply hiding the shell.

supported_inference: The removed reflected/Fresnel portion of the original combined glass closure contributes to the objectionable layering in these static views. A geometrically refracting nominal-IOR-1.38 shell alone does not recreate the visible band in this D setting.
unresolved: Reflection versus Fresnel transmission-weight coupling is not mathematically separated.
No unique scene object/light/environment reflection source was localized.
Single-GGX refraction replaces multi-GGX glass; energy and stochastic sampling differ.
No moving gaze, eyelid coverage, blink, new camera or production/Web performance has been tested.
acceptance: Not a delivery fix: flat dark eyes lack the required wet lively appearance. No independent C gate passed.
next_scope_candidate: A separately scoped wet-eye art candidate must decouple stable readable iris coloration from restrained optical reflection, preserving the sideward gaze and recovering a real catchlight without the broad band. Do not silently promote D, hide corneas in production, or paint catchlight pixels.
